I've got gstat and I know that it is possible to use sites file of GRASS, 
with x, y, and z coordinates. But  what is the best way to work with 3D data?
I would like to know if someone has used 3D data in GRASS and has 
interpolated these results to produce output maps. 
Some time ago I used GSTAT to produce 2D gaussian simulations and the output 
was writen in GRASS, but I can't imagine how to do this with 3D. Perhaps is 
it possible to produce a stack of raster maps? If so, how do I specify the 
vertical resolution of output (distance between maps)? Is this possible?

Perhaps it is better to use the GRASS Grid 3D Modules. But these are not 
compiled by default. Do they work right yet? Is it possible to use GSTAT to 
produce Grid3D maps?

messages.subject: [STATSGRASS] 3D geostatistics
messages.body_plain:
Javier,

you can "feed" gstat with 3D data in a sites list (haven't checked
this, but it should work); you can then interpolate on a series
of 2D (flat) grids, specifying the height of each grid layer by

set zmap=10.0; 
#    set height of mask map(s) to 10 when observations are 3-D. [0.0] 

or you can interpolate to a 3D grid, defined in a sites list, by using

data(): 'locations';
output: 'sites.out';

where 'locations' and 'sites.out' are the prediction locations and
output predictions sites lists, respectively.

Best regards,
--
Edzer

messages.in_reply_to: <20030528112638.C29404@itc.it>; from neteler@itc.it on Wed, May 28, 2003 at 11:26:38AM +0200
messages.body_plain:
(cc 'grass5' etc)

A suggestion arrived to protect the GRASS mailing list archives
from automated spam email address harvesters:

On Wed, May 28, 2003 at 11:26:38AM +0200, Markus Neteler wrote:
[...]
> On Tue, May 27, 2003 at 06:19:18PM -0700, Chuck Soper wrote:
> > Everyone must enter a generic 
> > username and password to search the web archives. Example: 
> > http://search.lists.apple.com/cocoa-dev
> 
> Ah - this is a nice idea.

OK, now I have added the same trick here.

All mailing list archives on grass.itc.it should be closed now for 
harvesters, but everybody can enter with the public password which
is printed in the authentication message (user: archives, pw: archives).

Thanks for this idea,

 Markus
